transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... I suppose I finally agreed to come in because... I just don't really care about things lately. The things that used to keep me balanced, anyway. 

Um. Like sailing races, or my Saturday shift at the historical society. Even just tinkering out in the woodshop... it all just feels like a chore now. I just keep putting it off. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy, like sailing races or working in the woodshop?
Yeah... like I just mentioned. I just don't care about them right now. The sailing, the woodshop... they're just chores I keep putting off. So, yes.
Do you feel down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day?
No... I wouldn't say that. I don't really feel sad, if that's what you mean. Just... what I mentioned before.
Do you feel more down or depressed in the evenings compared to other times of the day?
No... not really. I don't notice a difference. It's just... I'm not feeling depressed, like I said.
So you mentioned you don’t feel sad or depressed—can you describe more how you do feel, especially when you’re not engaging in those activities you used to enjoy?

I don't know. Just... flat, I guess. Like, my wife and kids might be laughing at dinner, or I'll finish a difficult milestone on a project at work... and I know I should feel good about those things. But mostly I just feel... I don't know, a little removed from it all. Just flat.
Have you noticed a decrease in your ability to feel pleasure, even in moments that you used to find enjoyable, like finishing a project or spending time with your family?
Yeah. I mean... like I just said. When they're laughing, or I get that work stuff done... I know I should feel good about it. But I don't really feel much of anything. Just... removed.
Can you recall the last time something really made you feel happy or excited, even a little bit?
Not really. I don't... I can't think of a specific time. It's just been a while, I guess.
Have you been feeling fatigued or lacking energy lately, even when you haven’t been doing much?
No... not really. I mean, I have enough energy. I still get my work done. It's not a physical tiredness, I guess. Just... what I said before.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating or focusing on tasks, even ones that you used to handle easily?
No. My focus is fine. Like I said, I still get my work done... concentrating isn't really a problem.
Would you say that you’ve completely lost interest in everything, or is there still something, even small, that you look forward to or enjoy?

I suppose it's... pretty much everything. That's actually what finally made me agree to come in. I just don't care about the things that used to keep me balanced. 

Um... sailing races, my Saturday shift at the historical society... even just tinkering out in the woodshop. It all just feels like a chore now. I just keep putting it off. So... no, not really anything I look forward to right now.
How long have you been feeling this way—this lack of interest and inability to feel pleasure?
It's been... a little over a year now. Since the accident with the scaffold, back when they were doing all that readjustment at the business. It just sort of started after that.
Have you had a continuously low mood for most of the day, more days than not, for at least the past two years?
No. Not two years. Like I said, it really just started after the accident last year. Before that... things were fine.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a lack of interest and pleasure (anhedonia) for over a year, with no significant low mood, no diurnal variation, no fatigue, and no concentration problems. This rules out major depressive disorder (F32.x) and persistent depressive disorder (F33.0-F33.3) due to duration and symptom profile. The lack of mood reactivity and chronic anhedonia supports a possible specifier of 'with pure anhedonia' in persistent depressive disorder (F33.4) or unspecified depressive disorder (F33.9).
